title: NATO in Ankara: Is Europe ready for a Russian attack? 🎙️ Independent Thinking podcast
summary: Chatham House podcast on the 2026 NATO Ankara summit: US retreat from European defence, a hardened Russian military that may test Article 5, and Europe's slow rearmament.

assertions.quote: the US cavalry no longer plans to come to rescue Europe.
the Prime Minister has said this himself, that Russia could attack NATO in 2030.
if Russia thinks that Article 5 is not going to hold, that they could, for example, try to attack a Baltic state.

verdicts.note: Intelligence services warn of this scenario, but no such attack has happened and forecasters put a Russia-NATO war in the next few years well under even odds.

assertions.quote: we are already subject to a lot of different hybrid attacks. And these hybrid attacks have intensified
Russia understands that it has a hardened transformed modernized military particularly in terms of land power

verdicts.note: Russia gained drone and combat experience and expanded production, but lost much of its pre-war equipment and trained manpower.

EFIS says Russia is building around 190 unmanned-systems battalions from Ukraine war lessons and expanding ammunition production seventeenfold, but also describes the army's moral decline, crime and pressured recruits.
US intelligence says Russia's ground forces have grown and its air and naval forces are arguably more capable than before the invasion, but does not attribute modernisation to combat experience.

assertions.quote: the German parliament actually, you know, passed a a special law to be able to take on more debt exclusively for rearmament
a lot of these capabilities are not necessarily going to come online in that same timeline.

verdicts.note: Many European programs deliver in the 2030s, after the 2029-30 window that threat assessments flag.

DDIS expects Russia's industry to keep out-producing Europe's and Russia to gain ground, 'especially if European countries fail to translate defence investment pledges into actual combat capabilities' fast enough: a risk, not a certainty.

assertions.quote: if the US really was to take action against Greenland, then that was going to be the end of NATO.
